title: Observational Equivalence in Count Branching DAGs with Mixed Poisson and Negative-Binomial Innovations
banked_reason: Delivered tier subfield below field floor; paper-score ceiling 7.0<7.4, with no bounded field-tier salvage after the near-Poisson soundness repair.
gap_reasons: The statistical contribution is substantially weaker: the whole-fiber upper bound has exponentially deteriorating zero-cell and genealogy constants, while the matching quadratic rate is proved only for a one-vertex simple-versus-simple experiment and transfers to the full class only as a converse.

The claim that the confidence output is evaluable and has polynomial delay is under-supported because no terminating interval-optimization algorithm or complexity analysis is supplied for the feasible-cell parameter and effect propagation.

The paper also supplies no implementation or stress evidence showing that the confidence procedure leaves its universal fallback at informative sample sizes, limiting its practical significance and projected leading-journal score.
proof_attempt_summary: The run established a specialized population package: complete strict mixed Poisson/NB observational fibers, legal reversal/root-choice structure, conditional parameter decoding, compelled arrows, and compressed single-treatment effect sets. It also proved conservative separated-class coverage and a sharp one-vertex quadratic benchmark whose converse transfers to containing mixed classes. The field-tier claim failed because practical full-DAG confidence remains unresolved: the available constants deteriorate exponentially, interval optimization lacks a terminating complexity analysis, and no implementation demonstrates informative finite-sample output.
tldr: For strict Bernoulli-thinning count DAGs whose independent innovations are nodewise positive Poisson or nondegenerate negative binomial with unknown labels, the population project seeks a degree-four, necessary-and-sufficient description of the entire observational fiber, its compelled arrows, and its compatible single-treatment effects. The established statistical result gives conservative whole-fiber coverage on separated compact generating subclasses. For local one-vertex fixed-mean Poisson-versus-negative-binomial testing, an explicit empirical-PGF test and a testing converse give matching sample-size order \(\Theta_{\mu,\eta}(\delta^{-2})\). Embedding that pair at an isolated vertex proves that only the quadratic lower bound transfers to uniformly accurate exact-fiber recovery, and to confidence sets required both to cover the truth and exclude the alternative, over the full mixed class and broader count-thinning classes containing the pair. No matching full-DAG upper bound is claimed; optimal dependence on dimension, graph structure, thinning, rare-cell mass, and simultaneous effect coverage remains open.
gap: Published PB-SCM results identify the all-Poisson recursive PGF and particular local directions, while Gao, Cai, and Hara prove uniqueness when every nonsink innovation is non-Poisson. Neither result characterizes the non-singleton observational fiber in the mixed regime where Poisson nonsinks coexist with negative-binomial anchors. Existing causal-effect enumeration and causal-order confidence-set methods concern Markov-equivalence or additive-error structures, not distribution equivalence created by thinning-law reversals.
fill: Prove or refute a degree-four complete-fiber theorem for every finite labeled strict mixed Poisson/negative-binomial branching DAG; if positive, establish the legal-reversal calculus, rational inverse, compact root-choice representation, local-size effect set, and simultaneous graph-set recovery theorem. The arbitrary-DAG genealogy and branch-decomposition arguments, not the finite audit, are the decisive obligations.
